Write the Arrow IPC formats

Source: R/write.R
arrow_write.Rd

arrow_write() writes a data frame, a struct array or a stream as an Arrow IPC file (format = "file", with a footer) or stream (format = "stream"). A path ending in .arrows defaults to the stream format; any other path, and x = NULL, to the file format.

Usage

arrow_write(
  data,
  x = NULL,
  format = c("file", "stream"),
  compression = c("none", "lz4", "zstd"),
  level = NULL,
  batch = 65536L,
  dictionary = TRUE,
  metadata = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, a struct array handle or a stream handle.

x

NULL to return the bytes, a path, or a connection.

format

"file" or "stream".

compression

"none", "lz4" or "zstd".

level

NULL for the codec's default, or a level on its scale.

batch

The most rows in one record batch, for a data frame.

dictionary

Whether factors are written as dictionaries.

metadata

NULL, or a named character vector of schema metadata.

Value

A raw vector when x is NULL, otherwise x, invisibly.

Details

A data frame is split into record batches of at most batch rows. Each factor is written as a dictionary with one dictionary batch before the first record batch, or as plain strings with dictionary = FALSE. Columns with arrow_extension, arrow_extension_metadata or arrow_field_metadata attributes keep them as field metadata, and metadata becomes the schema's custom metadata.

Bodies are padded to 8 bytes with zeros and are uncompressed by default, so every reader opens the file. compression = "lz4" writes LZ4 frames and "zstd" zstd frames through 'zukomp', at level on the codec's own scale; a buffer that does not shrink is written as it is. The same input and options give the same bytes on every platform.

See also

arrow_read().

Examples

df <- data.frame(x = 1:3, f = factor(c("a", "b", "a")))
bytes <- arrow_write(df, NULL)
arrow_read(bytes)
#>   x f
#> 1 1 a
#> 2 2 b
#> 3 3 a

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".arrows")
arrow_write(df, path, compression = "zstd")
arrow_read(path)
#>   x f
#> 1 1 a
#> 2 2 b
#> 3 3 a
